posts.cooked: We currently spend alot of time going through our amazon SC FBA orders, to get their inventory synced with what Amazon sells to what our Shopify Sells, and it is very tedious and overwhelming. What is the easy way to have orders imported from Amazon to Shopify, so that Inventory is reflected once they are sold on Amazon? We have used Marketplace connections, but the inventory does not sync for FBA orders, and importing the orders does not have an affect on the linked products we have on the Shopify store when they are sold on Amazon. I hope this makes sense.

Hi @DM_7

Connector apps often treat FBA inventory separately, causing sync issues. You need a dedicated multi-channel inventory app, not just a connector.

The easiest solution is to use Trunk. It connects to both Shopify and Amazon, acting as a central “brain.” When an item sells on Amazon FBA, Trunk instantly detects it and updates your Shopify inventory in real-time to match.

If you specifically need to import FBA orders into Shopify for reporting, use Amazon FBA Shipping (ByteStand). It is built for FBA logistics and will sync your Amazon stock levels back to your Shopify products automatically.

Hope this helps!

ai_summary.summarized_text:
The store’s central problem is that Amazon FBA sales do not automatically reduce linked Shopify inventory, even when orders are imported through a marketplace connector. This makes manual reconciliation time-consuming and risks inaccurate stock levels.

Suggested approaches include using a dedicated multi-channel inventory app such as Trunk to sync stock between Amazon and Shopify, or ByteStand’s Amazon FBA Shipping app if importing FBA orders into Shopify is also needed for reporting. A later reply offers a Shopify Flow designed to manage FBA inventory when using Marketplace Connect. Another response emphasizes first deciding whether FBA units should be available for sale through Shopify: if so, a tool must import orders and adjust Shopify stock; otherwise, FBA inventory should be excluded from Shopify’s available quantity.

No solution is confirmed as implemented, and the discussion leaves open which setup best fits the store’s needs. Several unrelated repeated posts about Amazon refunds do not address the inventory issue.
